(Capacity: 10,258) | champion = [[Wooden Legacy]] champions |tourney = [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = First Round }} {{2021–22 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2021–22 USC Trojans men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Southern California]] during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Trojans are led by 9th-year head coach [[Andy Enfield]] and played their home games at the [[Galen Center]] for the 16th season in [[Los Angeles]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. They finished the season 26–8, 14–6 in [[2021–22 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 Play]] to finish in third place. As the No. 3 seed in the [[2022 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]], they defeated [[2021–22 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] in the quarterfinals before losing in the semifinals to [[2021–22 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 7 seed in the Midwest Region, where they lost in the First Round to [[2021–22 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami (FL)]]. ==Previous season== {{see also|2020-21 USC Trojans men's basketball team}} The [[2020–21 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC Trojans]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] with a 25–8 overall record, and a 15–5 conference record. They finished in second place in the Pac-12 Conference. They were a part of the [[2021 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] they played against the [[2020-21 Utah Utes men's basketball team|Utah]] in the Quarterfinals and won in 2OT by the score of 91–85, they would move on to the semifinals but would lose to [[2020-21 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]] and would be eliminated from the tournament. They would then be invited to compete in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]] and would get wins against [[2020-21 Drake Bulldogs men's basketball team|Drake]], [[2020-21 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]], [[2020-21 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]], but would then be eliminated by the [[2020-21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga Bulldogs]] in the Elite Eight. ==Off-season== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- !Name !Number !Pos. !Height !Weight !Year !Hometown !Reason for Departure |- | Talin Lewis || 0 || G || 6'4" || 180 || Junior || [[Westlake Village, California|Westlake Village, CA]] || Walk-on; left the team |- | [[Tahj Eaddy]] || 2 || G || 6'2" || 165 || Redshirt Senior || [[West Haven, Connecticut|West Haven, CT]] || Declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]]; went [[Free agent|Undrafted]] |- | [[Evan Mobley]] || 4 || F || 7'0" || 215 || Freshman || [[Murrieta, California|Murrieta, CA]] || Declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]]; selected 3rd overall pick by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] |- | McKay Anderson || 14 || G || 6'5" || 190 || Redshirt Senior || [[La Cañada Flintridge, California|La Cañada, CA]] || Walk-on; graduated |- | Noah Baumann || 30 || G || 6'6" || 215 || Redshirt Junior || [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix, AZ]] || Transferred to [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] |} ===Incoming transfers=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
